S  directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  C482 No.458 of 2023  Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Priyanshu Gairola, Advocate, for the applicants.
Mr. Pankaj Joshi, Brief Holder, for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Prateek Tripathi, Advocate, holding brief of Mr. Siddhartha Bankoti, Advocate, for the respondent.

Respondent no.2, who is a complainant of the FIR No.446 of 2022, has registered the same as against the present applicants for their alleged involvement in commission of the offences under sections 498A, 323 and 504 of IPC, and section  of Dowry Prohibition Act.

After culmination of the investigation, and submission of the Chargesheet No.01, dated 27.10.2022,
the court of 1st, Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, had registered a Criminal Case No.508 of 2023, "State Vs. Rahul Uniyal and others", wherein, the present applicants have been summoned for the aforesaid offences by an order dated 21.01.2023.

entities.text: State Vs. Rahul Uniyal and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Its the chargesheet, the summoning order, and the proceedings, which are subject matter of challenge.

Since the matter is emanating from the matrimonial dispute, the parties have filed a compounding application along with C482 application, wherein, they have contended that since it is a matrimonial dispute and there happens to be a major misunderstanding amongst themselves.

The applicant no.1, upon being interacted by this Court has submitted, that owing to the certain unavoidable misunderstanding, which cannot be revealed, he has already initiated the proceedings under section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, which has been registered as HMA Petition No.1479 of 2022, "Sh. Rahul Uniyal and Smt. Aanchal Sharma".

In the compounding application it has been submitted, that they have agreed to settle their dispute on the payment of consolidated permanent alimony of Rupees Twenty Lakh, as a full and final settlement payable towards complainant/respondent no.2, which would be inclusive of the minor C482/458/2023 on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138822913/
1 child, who too has been agreed to be kept by respondent no.2.

Owing to the fact that the dispute has now reached up to the stage of Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, and the parties are open to participate in those proceedings, it will be absolutely a futile exercise to force upon the criminal proceedings upon them, and in order to patch up their differences for all times to come, let the proceedings under section 13B of the Act, itself take its call,
and be decided inter se rights on its merits.

Even upon being interacted the respondent no.2, too have expressed the same opinion that the complainant/respondent no.2, no more now intends to prosecute the present applicants for the alleged offences, which is being subject to the trial of Criminal Case No.508 of 2023, "State Vs.
Rahul Uniyal and others" pending consideration before the court of ACJM, 1, Dehradun.

entities.text:

Rahul Uniyal and others

sentences.text:
Owing to the candid statement, which has been made by the respective parties to the proceedings,
who are present in person, who have been duly identified by their respective counsels, coupled with the content of the compounding application, which too stands fortified by the signatures of the parties, as well as, that of the respective counsels.
The C482 application too would stands allowed, and as a consequence thereto the proceedings of the Criminal Case No.508 of 2023, "State Vs. Rahul Uniyal and others", pending consideration before the court of ACJM, 1, Dehradun, would hereby stands quashed.
